findings.title: Recovered-run polling stops after the first running verdict
findings.trigger: Reopen a persisted non-temporary conversation ending with a nonstreaming user message while its cloud run is active. The first liveness GET returns running.
findings.impact: The next scheduled poll skips the GET because the first verdict has set isLoading=true. No further timer is scheduled; the composer can remain busy after server completion or stall until another action resets it.
proof: shouldAskWhetherTurnIsRunning returns false when isLoading=true at inFlightTurnRecovery.ts46.
useChatStream.ts3600 passes store.isLoading;3614 sets it true after a running verdict and3616 schedules the next ask, which exits3605.
Ephemeral real-hook test advanced5001ms after the first running GET. Expected2 GETs, actual1. The first assertion confirmed actual store.isLoading=true.
findings.minimal_test: Mount the real persistent stream hook with a user-tail conversation and no owned stream. Return running then terminal/idle from successive run GETs. Advance the poll interval and require a second GET, busy=false on completion, and a stalled run surfaced as an error. Also test that a genuinely owned active stream does not create duplicate followers.
findings.validation_test: continues polling a recovered running turn and clears busy on completion
findings.limits: Client hook behavior is reproduced with deterministic fetch. No live server run or end-to-end browser was used.

findings.title: Stop on a recovered cloud turn never requests server cancellation
findings.status: client failure reproduced; durable lifecycle traced in source
findings.trigger: After reopening a cloud conversation whose liveness GET reports a running durable turn, press the visible Stop control before starting a new client-owned request.
findings.impact: Stop clears the local busy state but sends no run cancellation. The detached workflow may continue provider/tool execution and associated usage until its normal stop condition or another cancellation path.
proof: activeRunsRef starts empty at3502–3504 and receives handles only from consumeAssistantStream callbacks4162–4164/4455–4457. Reopen liveness recovery retains only a verdict and never installs the run handle.

stopGeneration only calls cancelCloudRunAndConfirm inside if(activeRun), but always stops local streaming/loading at4621–4622. abortConversation3511–3515 only aborts a controller in the separate client request map; recovery has no request controller there.
Ephemeral real-hook test asserted the running state, invoked stopGeneration and recorded all fetch calls. Expected POST to the returned run id, actual no POST.

The canonical run cancellation POST writes cancellation_requested_at through requestCloudAgentRunCancellation. The durable workflow is enqueued by workflow/api start, with no request signal in StartCloudAgentWorkflowExecutionInput; the invocation owns an AbortController and reads the DB cancellation flag at each loop check.
findings.minimal_test: Mount a restored running conversation, retain the authenticated run handle, click Stop, require cancellation POST for that run and poll confirmed terminal state. Use a durable workflow fixture independent of the browser request to assert the persisted cancellation flag halts a future provider/tool dispatch; require a visible failure if cancellation cannot be confirmed.
findings.validation_test: sends a cancellation for the recovered cloud run when Stop is pressed
findings.limits: The absence of the client cancellation call is reproduced. Continued live billing/tool execution was not observed; it follows from the source-owned durable lifecycle and is a conditional impact.

findings.title: Reopening a cached chat discards newer persisted messages
findings.status: reproduced against current integrated conversation hook and store
findings.trigger: Open a previously cached, nonstreaming conversation after a different device or durable server run has added persisted messages. The successful conversation-detail response contains a newer transcript.
findings.impact: The fresh transcript is parsed but discarded whenever any local cached message exists. Reopening still displays the stale transcript, and the next user turn can operate with missing remote context.
proof: loadConversation fetches and parses current paginated server messages, maps them to messages, then immediately returns at599–601 if cachedMessages.length>0. setActiveConversationWithMessages604–608 only runs for an empty cache.
Ephemeral real-hook test cached one old message, returned two valid server messages, explicitly asserted loadConversation returned true, and observed only the old message in the real store.

Inspected web artifact cloud-sync reads the shared sync response but only applies artifacts; it does not compensate by merging chat messages. The server durable settlement does persist the completed assistant turn.
findings.minimal_test: Cache a completed conversation, serve a valid response with an additional message, reopen it and require the new persisted message while preserving the locally selected valid branch leaf. Cover remote edits/deletes and protect the actual locally streaming transcript from stale network snapshots.
findings.validation_test: merges fresh server messages into a cached nonstreaming conversation on reopening
findings.limits: Reopen freshness failure is reproduced. Live cross-device sync, message conflict policy and every possible compensating handler were not exhaustively tested.

findings.title: Channel preference refuses unrelated browser work when any structured connector is offered
findings.status: source-confirmed behavior; product policy premise needs root disposition
findings.trigger: A durable turn has Gmail/send-email or another structured connector plus browser-automation/navigate, and tries to visit an unrelated website that the structured connector cannot handle.
findings.impact: The browser step is refused as if the connector can perform the same work. Merely connecting a structured integration can disable unrelated browser/automation capability during the run.
proof: preferredAlternativeTo compares only execution channel rankings across every offered tool, with no argument, service or capability match.
Durable invocation builds this gate from all connector-origin tool definitions and invokes refusalFor before dispatch.
The existing test72–77 explicitly expects Gmail/send-email to refuse browser/navigate and therefore codifies this blanket behavior rather than testing equivalent work.
findings.minimal_test: With allowed Gmail send-email and browser navigate, allow browser navigation to an unrelated research site; separately require the typed connector for genuinely equivalent email work. A denied email action must remain impossible through browser automation, so the fix needs capability-scoped denial equivalence rather than weakening permission checks.
findings.limits: No additional runtime test executed for this candidate. Current tests intentionally encode the behavior; root should decide whether blanket account-wide refusal is an explicit product requirement before registering it as a defect.

findings.title: Managed-compute enforcement test accepts denials from different gates
findings.trigger: Managed compute is configured off, but its admission gate is bypassed while a spend or model gate still rejects the request.
findings.impact: The test can pass without proving the specific managed-compute policy is enforced, despite claiming to rule out earlier gates. This weakens enterprise admission evidence.
proof: The accepted response pattern at97 is managed_compute_disabled|over_cap|model_blocked. over_cap/model_blocked do not establish the intended managed-compute gate.
Status402 or403 at90–93 is likewise shared by unrelated refusals; there is no positive control for the same admitted model/budget request in this case.
findings.minimal_test: Construct an otherwise admitted request with adequate budget and an allowed model; require the exact managed_compute_disabled code when the policy is off, then enable the policy and require that this gate permits the same request. Inject a broken managed-compute gate and prove the test fails even if another refusal remains.
findings.limits: The e2e suite was not run and no runtime enforcement bypass is claimed.
